findings.evidence: Confirmed `@[expose]` hits at `Partitions.lean:33,87,123,132` and `Conjugate.lean:158`; the corresponding characteristic lemmas occur at lines 39, 94, 137, and 163 respectively.
findings.fix: Remove all five `@[expose]` attributes and use the existing `rowLens_diagramOf`, `parts_toPartition`, `shapePartition_parts`, and `diagramOf_conjugate` APIs; add a specific lemma wherever a consumer still needs an unsupported observation.
findings.issue: The bodies of `diagramOf`, `toPartition`, `shapePartition`, and `partitionEquivYoungDiagram`, plus `conjugate` in `Conjugate.lean:158`, are marked `@[expose]` despite public extensional lemmas characterizing their results.

findings.evidence: The definition’s `toFun` and `invFun` are at lines 125–126, while the only nearby inverse lemmas characterize the standalone constructors (`toPartition_diagramOf` and `diagramOf_toPartition`), not applications of the equivalence.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp]` apply and symm-apply lemmas identifying the two directions with `⟨diagramOf μ, card_diagramOf μ⟩` and `toPartition μ.1 μ.2`, then keep the equivalence body unexposed.
findings.issue: `partitionEquivYoungDiagram` has no simp lemmas describing either its forward application or inverse application, so consumers must unfold the exposed equivalence body to connect it with `diagramOf` and `toPartition`.

summary: The refactor unnecessarily exposes implementation bodies and leaves the rebuilt equivalence without characteristic application lemmas.
